title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth projective surface and Y a smooth hyperplane section, so Y is a curve. Superscript 1 means codimension-1 cycles. A^1 = Pic (codimension-1 cycles modulo rational equivalence), J^1 = Pic^0 (Picard variety, or Jacobian for Y), NS^1 = Néron–Severi group. The previous page is headed 'Conjectures de Lefschetz pour cycles algébriques'. This page tests what a Lefschetz-type hyperplane theorem for Chow groups modulo rational equivalence (not just modulo homological equivalence) could say in the first non-trivial case: divisors on a surface restricted to a curve.

(1) NS^1(X) -> NS^1(Y) = Z, given by D -> deg(D|Y) = D.H. The image has finite index and the kernel has rank rho - 1. This is the primitive part of NS (my reading of 'rang rho-1').

(2) J^1(X) = Pic^0(X) -> J^1(Y) = Jac(Y) is injective except for p-torsion. This is the Lefschetz/Weil fact that the Picard variety embeds in the Jacobian of an ample curve, up to a finite, possibly infinitesimal, kernel in characteristic p.

(3) A^1(X) = Pic(X) -> A^1(Y) = Pic(Y) has kernel K. Since K ∩ Pic^0(X) is finite and NS(X) is finitely generated, K is finitely generated.

(4) Let B^1(X) be the subgroup of Pic(X) of classes whose restriction to Y has degree 0. It maps to J^1(Y) and contains K. Put M^1(X) = B^1(X)/J^1(X); this is the primitive Néron–Severi group, of rank rho - 1. The map induces K -> M^1(X) -> J^1(Y)/Im J^1(X). The first arrow is injective modulo a finite group. The target, the quotient of Jac(Y) by the image of Pic^0(X), is called the 'partie mobile' (variable part) of the Jacobian. So K is, up to finite groups, the kernel of a homomorphism from primitive NS to the variable part of Jac(Y), an Abel–Jacobi/normal-function type map. A question is crossed out: is an element of M^1 with zero image in K?

(5) N.B.: Grothendieck says that 'in general' M^1(X) -> J(Y)/J(X) is injective modulo a finite group, hence K is finite. He presumes this holds when the hyperplane sections in general pencils containing Y are irreducible. Read for the generic member Y_eta of a pencil, this is a Shioda–Tate-type statement. Blow up the base points to get a fibration X~ -> P^1. If D restricts trivially to Y_eta, then D is a combination of fibre components. With all fibres irreducible, only multiples of the fibre class H remain, and H|Y has degree H^2 ≠ 0. So K is finite. Reducible fibres are exactly what would produce a kernel, as in the 'trivial lattice' correction of the Shioda–Tate formula.
errors: The N.B. and the 'presumption' cannot hold for every base field or every special Y. Over the algebraic closure of a finite field, J(Y)(k) is a torsion group. The free group M^1(X), of rank rho - 1, then maps to a torsion group, so its kernel has finite index. Hence K has rank rho - 1, whatever the irreducibility of the members of the pencils. Irreducibility of pencil members is therefore not sufficient. The statement needs Y generic (the generic member over k(t)) or very general over an uncountable field. Over number fields one needs Silverman/Néron-type specialization, which excludes a thin set.

Small slip: the restriction Pic^0(X) -> Jac(Y) for an ample curve Y has finite kernel in general. 'Injectif exc. p' is accurate only when Y is sufficiently ample, for example a very ample hyperplane section with suitable vanishing.

ideas.what: Lefschetz-type restriction of Pic, Pic^0 and NS from a surface to an ample curve; the kernel K of Pic(X)->Pic(Y) is finitely generated
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz theorem for Picard groups / Grothendieck–Lefschetz
ideas.where_published: SGA 2 (Lefschetz theorems for Pic), FGA Picard schemes

ideas.what: Factor the kernel through a map from primitive NS(X) to the 'variable part' J(Y)/Im Pic^0(X) of the Jacobian of the section
ideas.modern_name: Abel–Jacobi / normal function of primitive divisor classes; Mordell–Weil group of the Jacobian fibration of a Lefschetz pencil
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (normal functions); Shioda (Mordell–Weil lattices for higher-genus fibrations, 1990s)

ideas.what: Presumption that K is finite (Pic(X)->Pic(Y) injective mod finite) when members of general pencils through Y are irreducible
ideas.modern_name: Shioda–Tate formula (trivial lattice correction by reducible fibres); Noether–Lefschetz for curve sections; Moishezon / Ravindra–Srinivas type injectivity

missed.claim: Grothendieck relates the Lefschetz question for Chow groups of divisors to the Mordell–Weil group of the Jacobian of hyperplane sections modulo the fixed part. He identifies irreducibility of members of pencils as the criterion for injectivity. This is the content of the Shioda–Tate trivial-lattice correction, here in the context of Lefschetz conjectures for cycles.
missed.quote: Je présume qu'il en est ainsi si les sections hyperplanes de Y dans les pinceaux généraux contenant Y sont des courbes irréductibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links Lefschetz-type statements for Chow groups (Bloch–Beilinson / Lefschetz standard conjecture circle) with Mordell–Weil lattices of Lefschetz pencils, and shows how such statements depend on the base field (they fail over the algebraic closure of F_p). It is mainly of historical interest; the mathematics is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: A short, partly speculative sketch. It frames Lefschetz for divisors modulo rational equivalence via the 'variable part' of the Jacobian and anticipates the Shioda–Tate-type role of reducible fibres. Both are known today (Shioda, Moishezon, Ravindra–Srinivas), and the presumption as stated fails over the algebraic closure of a finite field.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 appears to read 'NS^1(X) -> NS^1(Y) surjectif mod. groupe fini, noyau de rang rho-1' (or similar), not 'Pic^tau(X) -> Pic^tau(Y)'. The 'noyau de rang rho-1' reading of the second line is plausible from the image.
Line 3 appears to be 'A^1(X) -> A^1(Y)' (Chow/Pic modulo rational equivalence), not NS^1. Its kernel K satisfies 'K ∩ J^1(X) fini, donc K de type fini'.
'Pic^1(X)' in the definition of B^1(X) is probably 'A^1(X)'. The sense is 'classes de diviseurs dont la restriction à Y est de degré 0'.
The crossed-out passage reads approximately: 'Question: un élément de M^1(X) dont l'image dans J^1(Y)/J^1(X) est nulle, est-il dans [image de] K ...'.
'non sing.' in lines 1–2 is written 'non sing.' (rendered as 'un sing.' by the machine).
